ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against the Consolidated United Nations Security Council Sanctions List, the Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List administered by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act list, the Office of Foreign Assets Control Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (for any USD-clearing or United States nexus), the UK HM Treasury Consolidated List (for GBP or SWIFT rails), and the European Union Common Foreign and Security Policy consolidated list (for EUR correspondent banking). Politically exposed persons are assessed under the definitions in S.O.R./2002-184, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs and heads of international organizations; enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth analysis and senior-management approval are required for any PEP or elevated-risk hit. Adverse-media and negative-news checks are mandatory. Findings material to the entity's banking relationship must be documented and, where the entity becomes a reporting entity under the PCMLTFA, suspicious transaction reports must be filed with FINTRAC; otherwise the obligor bank will apply these measures as part of customer due diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: British Columbia Corporate Online ('BC Corporate Online') operated by the Registrar of Companies, BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance; https://bc-corporateonline.gov.bc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be set out in English or French, or both, using Latin characters only; the BC Corporate Registry does not accept non-Latin script such as Chinese characters. Where a foreign-language trade name is desired, a transliterated or translated equivalent must be recorded in the corporate filing. The name must be distinctive, not merely descriptive, and must not be confusingly similar to an existing company, extraprovincial company, trademark or registered name under ss. 24 and 26 of the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia). An unlimited liability company must include the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Company' or the abbreviation 'ULC' as its designated legal ending.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: bank, banking, bancaire (unless licensed under the Financial Institutions Act)
insurance, assurance, reinsurance (unless licensed under the Insurance Act)
university, college, school, institute (unless authorized under provincial education statutes)
chamber of commerce, board of trade (reserved)
law society, lawyer, barrister, solicitor (professional regulator words)
engineer, engineering, architecture, architectural (triggers the Engineers and Geoscientists of British Columbia or Architectural Institute of British Columbia authorization)
Canada, Canadian, Government, Crown, British Columbia (implies sovereign or public agency affiliation)
cooperative, co-op (reserved under the Cooperative Association Act)
International, World, Global, Pacific (highly sensitive; requires supporting evidence of geographic scope)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A BC name reservation may be extended once by filing a Name Reservation Extension under B.C. Reg. 221/2004, adding a further 56 days, for a maximum cumulative reservation of 112 days. If the reservation expires, a new Name Reservation must be submitted. Where the Registrar rejects a name for lack of distinctiveness or confusing similarity under s. 24 BCBCA, the applicant may: (i) file a revised Name Reservation with a fresh distinctive element; (ii) submit a formal Name Reconsideration Request through the BC Registry Contact Centre attaching trademark search evidence or a NUANS-style search report within 30 days of rejection; (iii) apply for judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, within 60 days of the Registrar's written refusal where the decision is patently unreasonable or procedurally flawed; (iv) if the rejection arises from a third-party objection filed under s. 25 BCBCA, provide written submissions to the Registrar for disposition under s. 26, and the Registrar may direct a name change or cancel the objection. For complex or ministerial-approval names, a prescribed Corporate Name Approval Request (Form 1) may be filed instead of a standard online reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only where the virtual-office provider maintains a physical street address in British Columbia that the Registrar of Companies may use for service of process and where the registered records office duties under ss. 28-29 BCBCA can be fulfilled. A post office box is prohibited. For a non-reporting engineering-design ULC with no physical employees in British Columbia, a registered-agent arrangement is commercially accepted; however, the transparency register and statutory books must be physically accessible at that office, and the registered office must accept legal service during ordinary business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk, approximately 5% per year for this non-regulated, non-reporting private ULC engaged in offshore BIM/CAD drafting. The BC Registrar may demand production of records under s. 291 BCBCA and regulators may conduct inspections upon complaint or suspicious-activity triggers, but FINTRAC does not routinely inspect non-reporting entities and the BC Corporate Registry does not conduct random unannounced on-site inspections of unregulated private companies engaged in engineering design services.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), S.B.C. 2002, c. 57; s. 3 (company with unlimited liability), Part 2 (incorporation, ss. 10-22), s. 51 (shareholder liability in ULC), and s. 88 (certificate correction).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (Corporate Online portal: corporateonline.gov.bc.ca).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles and Articles, filed under s. 10 of the BCA; Certificate of Incorporation issued under s. 12 of the BCA.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement and no statutory escrow or deposit. The Company may issue common shares for nominal consideration. Shareholders of a ULC remain fully liable for company debts under s. 51(2) of the BCA.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company as an unlimited liability company under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) is hereby ratified. The share subscription of the initial shareholder is accepted, and 1,000 common shares with nominal value are issued. The registered office at [street address], Vancouver, British Columbia, is adopted, and [name] is appointed as registered records agent. The following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer. The financial institution providing the operating account is designated. All applicable filing and administrative authorities are delegated. Legal counsel is instructed to complete post-incorporation filings and obtain any required tax registrations. These resolutions are effective as of the date of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services - Corporate Online Name Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use Corporate Online to verify the proposed name is distinguishable and complies with the BC Company Name Regulation. For an ULC, include a legal element such as 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company'. Submit a name reservation if a NUANS report is required or the name is unusual.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, use Corporate Online's reconsideration channel or submit a revised name application. Refusal may be judicially reviewed, but a revised name is generally faster.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and initial directors (through legal counsel or authorized service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles, including the ULC designation and authorized share structure. Prepare the Notice of Articles with the registered office address and initial directors. Obtain a signed Consent to Act as Director from each director. Confirm each director is an individual over 18, not bankrupt, and not of unsound mind.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Pre-filing deficiencies are cured by amending the draft documents. If a director is disqualified, replace that director and obtain a new consent before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to Corporate Online, select incorporation of an unlimited liability company, enter the approved name, complete the Notice of Articles, upload the signed Articles, and pay the electronic filing fee of CA$350 (approximately US$255). The system validates the submission and issues the electronic Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries or rejects the filing, correct the deficiency through the Corporate Online platform under s. 10(4) BCA, or withdraw and refile without a penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Certified Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and Company Summary from Corporate Online. Verify the legal name, incorporation date, registration number, and registered office address. Begin the corporate minute book by placing the certificate, Notice of Articles, and director consents in the official records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a registry error, submit a correction application under s. 88 BCA. If the certificate is lost or corrupted, order a certified replacement via Corporate Online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Company Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or sign a written consent resolution. Adopt the pro forma First Board Resolution, issue share certificates to the subscriber, appoint officers, adopt by-laws if desired, and keep the registered office records current. Register for a federal Business Number, GST/HST, and payroll accounts with the Canada Revenue Agency, and open a corporate bank account.
required_dossiers: Written resolutions of the first board
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Governance omissions can be cured by supplementary ordinary or extraordinary resolutions, or by filing late or corrected records with the corporate registry and tax authorities within the applicable cure period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial establishment or manufacturing facility is required for ISIC 7110 / NAICS 541330 CAD/BIM civil infrastructure services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required; the business operates as a professional engineering drafting and BIM outsourcing service without physical plant licensing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (Environmental Assessment Office and Permitting Branch)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no physical facility, no land disturbance, and no emissions or effluent sources attributable to the registered service activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater, VOC emissions, or commercial waste-handling obligations apply. The office lease, if any, must comply with municipal sewer, solid waste, and building ventilation by-laws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for white-collar CAD/BIM consulting. Any leased office must obtain an occupancy certificate and pass the local fire safety inspection (e.g., City of Vancouver Fire and Building Inspection Services). Ongoing occupational safety for employees is governed by the Workers Compensation Act (BC) and enforced by WorkSafeBC.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — GST/HST and Business Number (BN) programme. Portals: Business Registration Online (BRO) at www.canada.ca/business-registration, GST/HST NETFILE for electronic filing, and My Business Account (MyBA) for account administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The BC ULC must obtain a statutory 9-digit CRA Business Number (TIN) and a GST/HST program account (BN suffix 'RT') by filing Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts' via Business Registration Online (BRO), or by fax/mail to the CRA Sudbury Tax Centre. A non-resident ULC (deemed non-resident under ITA 250(5.1)) must identify its Canadian permanent establishment or appointed agent for service on Form RC1. Registration for GST/HST is mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold (measured over the preceding four calendar quarters); voluntary registration is permitted from the first taxable supply and is strategically advantageous for zero-rated exporters because it enables full recovery of input tax credits. The CRA may require security from a non-resident registrant lacking a Canadian establishment (ETA 240).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) US federal check-the-box election (Form 8832): the BC ULC is an eligible entity and may elect partnership or disregarded-entity status for US tax purposes. (2) Canadian deemed non-residence under ITA 250(5.1)-(5.2): automatic where the ULC is a wholly-owned subsidiary of a non-resident corporation and was incorporated or continued in a designated jurisdiction (British Columbia is designated), subject to statutory anti-avoidance conditions; the ULC is then treated as non-resident for Part I tax with exposure limited to Canadian-source income and Part XIII withholding. (3) ETA 273 election for nil consideration on supplies between closely related registrants, where applicable. There is no separate hybrid-mismatch election under the Excise Tax Act; the ULC remains a corporation for GST/HST purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA). British Columbia does not impose HST or PST on exported engineering/BIM services; BC PST (7%) applies only to tangible personal property, certain software, and prescribed taxable services delivered in BC, none of which apply to offshore CAD/BIM deliverables.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies (small-supplier threshold, ETA 148(1)); the threshold is measured over the preceding four calendar quarters and applies equally to non-resident suppliers without a Canadian establishment. Registration is mandatory once exceeded; voluntary registration is available below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, government API invoicing, or digital stamping. GST/HST registrants must issue invoices containing prescribed information (ETA 223), but invoices are neither pre-cleared nor validated by the CRA. Electronic filing of GST/HST returns is mandatory for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million, with monthly or quarterly reporting periods. Peppol-based e-invoicing is voluntary and not integrated with CRA fiscal clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, section 9 to a supply of a service made to a non-resident, provided the non-resident is not registered for GST/HST, does not carry on business in Canada at the relevant time, and the service is not performed in respect of (i) real property situated in Canada, (ii) tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, or (iii) intangible personal property usable only in Canada. Offshore BIM and structural drafting deliverables transmitted electronically to a non-resident EPC client qualify for zero-rating under section 9. Input tax credits on Canadian inputs (software subscriptions, CAD workstations, office overhead) are fully recoverable by a registrant whose supplies are zero-rated, generating net refunds. The BC ULC, whether resident or deemed non-resident under ITA 250(5.1), must obtain and retain evidence of the client's non-resident status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed export services contract / Statement of Work specifying BIM and structural drafting deliverables for offshore civil infrastructure projects
Commercial invoice annotated 'Zero-rated export pursuant to ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s.9'
Non-resident status evidence of the client (foreign tax identification number, tax residence certificate, or statutory declaration of non-residence)
Payment evidence: SWIFT MT103 wire transfer receipt or Wise business payment confirmation
Deliverable transmission records (digital handoff logs, IP transmission receipts, download records for CAD/BIM files)
GST/HST returns and input tax credit working papers substantiating zero-rating and ITC allocation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline for export proceeds; zero-rating eligibility is not contingent on repatriation timing. The CRA reassessment window is 4 years (ETA 298), extended to 7 years for neglect, misrepresentation, or fraud. If zero-rating is denied (for example, the client is found to be GST-registered, carrying on business in Canada, or services relate to Canadian realty), the CRA assesses 5% GST on the full supply, disallows related ITCs, and charges arrears interest (ETA 280). Penalties include 50% of the tax sought to be evaded for knowingly or grossly negligently making a false statement (ETA 285); fines up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment, or CAD 25,000 and up to 2 years on summary conviction, for evading GST (ETA 327-328); and director liability for unremitted amounts (ETA 323). Books and records substantiating export zero-rating must be retained for 6 years (ETA 286).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC); foreign-exchange monitoring and anti-money-laundering surveillance administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); prudential oversight of federally regulated banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is a freely convertible currency under the IMF Article VIII framework; Canada maintains no exchange-control restrictions on current or capital account transactions. For the British Columbia Unlimited Liability Corporation, the principal converting-and-remittance hurdle is not FX regulation but the income tax characterization of the entity and potential Part XIII withholding tax on certain non-resident payments, specifically dividends, interest, royalties, and management fees. The ULC's pass-through eligibility must be managed so that repatriation of contributed surplus and return of capital is clearly documented as non-taxable, while any deemed or actual dividend is reconciled against transactional creditors and CRA filings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio exist under Canadian law. Export revenue generated by the CAD-BIM services may be held in USD or other convertible foreign currency, converted through commercial banking channels, or applied directly against foreign-currency supplier and contractor liabilities. The ULC must nevertheless preserve source-based invoicing, SWIFT narrative references, and bank statements that demonstrate such proceeds are genuine earned professional fees rather than unexplained inbound payments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD dual-currency); Capital Escrow Account for contributed surplus where a lender requires segregation
Operational Account; international clearing via SWIFT and Lynx
Operational Account; treasury management and foreign exchange desk
Capital Escrow Account; Corporate operating sub-account
Operational Account with same-day Lynx clearing for CAD disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. A fully regulated cross-border fintech or electronic money institution is a supplement only and cannot replace a Canadian bank for the CA_ULC because corporate account opening, Lynx membership, and credible treasury clearing require a Canadian bank or credit union. Services such as Wise are viable for low-value vendor disbursements, employee reimbursements, and micro FX conversions, provided the fintech holds a FINTRAC money-services-business registration, maintains customer funds segregated, and can produce transaction reconciliation exports. Offshore digital EMIs that lack FINTRAC registration must not be used, as such usage materially increases AML-KYC blocking risk and may justify a bank account termination by a Schedule I lender.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian Tier-1 commercial banks generally permit remote onboarding of a British Columbia ULC when the directors are non-resident, subject to submission of notarized banking resolutions, apostilled certificate of incorporation and certificate of status, current register of directors, persons-with-significant-control (PSC) register, and a complete AML questionnaire evidencing commercial substance in BC. Banks retain the discretionary mandate to require a physical or video-identification interview of at least one director or officer, and in practice a visit to a Vancouver branch by the authorized signatory or a relationship-manager site visit is often required for unlimited liability entities. The recommended defence is appointment of one Canadian-resident universal signatory while all non-resident directors remain fully disclosed as KYC-authorized principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC substantially unlimited liability and pass-through/tax-transparent tax classification perceived as a hybrid-mismatch or opaque-flow-through structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRA technical interpretation or legal opinion on the ULC's Canadian tax classification; shareholder consent and unlimited-liability waiver forms; audited inner-hold financial statements for the ULC; lease agreement, payroll records, and service infrastructure demonstrating physical and operational substance in BC; intercompany service agreement and transfer-pricing documentation supporting the invoicing of CAD-BIM deliverables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors resident in multiple or higher-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of passports; citizenship and tax-residency certificates; PEP declarations for every director and PSC; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for asset contributions; legal opinion confirming no bearer-share or nominee-shareholder arrangements; current BC corporate register search (Corporate Online) and a stamped PSC register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border CAD-BIM revenue concentrated among a small group of foreign clients or related parties, creating concern of disguised trade payments or round-tripped capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed engineering-services agreements; itemized invoices with CAD model, BIM file delivery, or drafting milestone references; time sheets and deliverable-existence records; beneficial owner and payment-history verification; third-party confirmation from the client’s bank; multi-year pricing and work-product explanation showing business rationality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of fintech rails, multiple foreign accounts, or third-party payment platforms for disbursement of earned revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full transaction-level export from the fintech/wallet platform; reconciliation reports tied to the ULC's ERP timesheet and invoicing system; signed remitter/beneficiary authorizations; provider’s FINTRAC MSB licence and its affirmation of segregated safeguarding; summary of currency conversion rates and fees; bank reference letters for each counterparty wallet.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for CA_ULC from a foreign parent or direct beneficial owner must be wired through SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 payment using a Schedule I bank or a reputable foreign bank. The wire narrative must clearly state in capital letters 'ULC CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — NON-BORROWED EQUITY / DEMANDE DE CAPITAL', together with the entity legal name, BC registration number, and a transaction reference that matches the board resolution and PSC declarations. All injections above CAD 10,000 are captured automatically by the bank’s FINTRAC large-cash transaction reporting obligation. Verification standards require the inbound wire beneficiary legal name to match the account title exactly; beneficial-owner identity to remain consistent with KYC files; no unassigned corporate treasury accounts; and the payment to expressly disclaim lender/debt status, thereby confirming an equity contribution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Permitted clearing rail hierarchy for trade settlements and disbursements: (a) SWIFT MT103/MT202 and ISO 20022 for cross-border USD, EUR, GBP, and JPY payments; (b) Lynx high-value payment system for same-day CAD clearing for time-critical contractor suppliers; (c) Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for routine weekly payroll and recurring Canadian vendor payments; (d) Commercial Letters of Credit governed by UCP600 where the counterparty requires documentary proof of delivery for CAD-BIM milestones; and (e) Wise or equivalent FINTRAC-registered EMI for de minimis disbursement under CAD 2,000, subject to treasury manual review. Every outbound instruction must include a compliant purpose narrative, e.g., 'Professional services — engineering drafting' or 'Subcontract compensation for continental construction drafting work', to prevent banking-compliance referral and preserve audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot foreign-exchange transactions with a Schedule I or Schedule III bank for same-day CAD/USD conversion of operational receipts
Outright vanilla forward contracts for committed USD/CAD cash flows, typically 1- to 6-month tenors
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for CAD/USD where bilateral net cash settlement is preferable to physical delivery
Cross-currency swaps (fixed/floating or fixed/fixed) for long-dated construction and infrastructure contracts in USD,CAD,or EUR
Vanilla foreign-exchange options (call and put) for protecting margin on material CAD/BIM outsourcing contracts where exact settlement timing is uncertain
Rolling spot conversion and layered micro-forwards managed under a documented treasury hedging policy approved by the ULC board

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under s.274 of the BC Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Ministry of Finance / BC Business Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the anniversary date of incorporation; e.g., a 15 June incorporation must file by 14 August each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100; continued non-filing after the 2-month window permits the Registrar to administratively strike off or dissolve the company; restoration within 10 years requires payment of all arrears and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and BC provincial corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and BC Ministry of Finance under consolidated T2 system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the ULC's fiscal year-end; a calendar 31 December year-end is due by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; higher penalties apply to repeated or grossly negligent failures, plus daily interest and director liability for unremitted amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T106 Information Return for Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the ULC's tax year-end, concurrent with the T2 deadline; required when reportable cross-border non-arm's length transactions exceed CAD 1,000,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty under s.162(7) of CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500; repeated or egregious filings may attract higher penalties and transfer-pricing adjustments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (applicable if registered or where online supply exceeds registrant thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the ULC's fiscal year-end for annual GST/HST filers; a calendar 31 December fiscal year is due by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late-filing penalty of 1% of unremitted net tax for 1-4 days, plus 0.25% per complete month up to 12 months, and prescribed daily interest on the outstanding balance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size or revenue threshold triggers a compulsory audit under the BCBCA. A private BC ULC must appoint an auditor at each AGM unless all shareholders consent annually to waive the auditor under s.206 of the BCBCA. A BC public company or a subsidiary of a public company cannot waive the appointment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is the default for a private BC ULC; IFRS is permitted and mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises. The T2 return applies Income Tax Act adjustments to GAAP; financial statements are only filed with CRA when explicitly requested.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual review date, the directors must verify that the transparency register identifies every individual with significant control (direct or indirect ownership or control of at least 25% of voting or value rights). All share transfers in the prior year are reconciled against the register of members, and the transparency register is amended within 30 days of any change. No separate UBO return is submitted to the BC Registrar; the BC Annual Report includes a statutory declaration that the company's records, including the transparency register, are accurate and available for inspection by enforcement authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders' and directors' meetings
Transparency Register of Individuals with Significant Control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined general corporate rate (15% federal Part I plus 12% British Columbia general corporate tax).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays in Canada. Effective rate may be reduced by federal SR&ED investment tax credits (15% of qualifying Canadian R&D expenditures for non-CCPCs) and the British Columbia R&D tax credit (generally 10% of eligible expenditures). A foreign-controlled ULC is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation and cannot claim the small business deduction.
